Diplomatic Transcript of the *Vajradhātumukhākhyāna* (The Explanation of the Face of the Vajra Realm)
Péter-Dániel Szántó, 2009-01-15, Bombay [page 01]
[Wooden Cover] [Page 02] # [Image] *Śrīmad Vajrasat Guru*, etc. I pay homage to the glorious Vajrasattva, the world...

To the supreme Guru, the source of all Buddhas; who, through various forms, has manifested as the remover of the three fears, abiding upon Mount Meru; the support of the Dharma for the Munis, auspicious with the qualities of the Jinas; the mandala of the Vajradhātu; whose single form is all-encompassing, the supreme Śiva.
—[I offer this] for the sake of the liberation of embodied beings. Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature;

I am pure by nature. Having generated oneself as the self-nature of the conviction in selflessness, through the transformation of the syllable *hūṃ* into a vajra, one becomes oneself a vajra-blazing fire.

One should meditate on the deity: blue in color, with eight arms and four faces. With the two primary arms, he performs the gesture of embracing the Prajñā with a vajra and a vajra-bell. With another pair of arms, he holds a sword and a noose with the threatening gesture (*tarjanī*). With another pair of arms...

He holds a wheel and a *khaṭvāṅga* with his other two hands, and carries an arrow and a bow. His principal face is black, the right is white, the left is red, and the rear is yellow; each face has three eyes. Adorned with ornaments of serpents, he stands in the *pratyālīḍha* posture, treading upon Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī. Meditate on him in a wrathful form, adorned with all [the appropriate] ornaments.

—t. At the throat, with the syllable *raktahrīḥ*, one should produce an eight-petaled lotus. With the syllable *hūṃ* upon a lotus petal, one should produce a five-pronged vajra for the tongue: *oṃ vajrajihva*. With the syllable *a* in both hands, one should produce two moon disks; upon these— [page 04]
Having fashioned two five-pronged [vajras] from the syllables *ra* and *hūṃ*, one should perform the binding of the fingers and the destruction of obstacles with the excellent thread, and so forth.
Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ vaṃ.
Oṃ guhya vajrasamaya vaṃ.
Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka abhiṣiñca māṃ.
[page 05] Oṃ tuṃ 3 || Oṃ vajra tuṣya ho ||
oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ || oṃ vajrānala daha paca matha daha bhañja raṇa hūṃ phaṭ || [page 06]
Oṃ vajranetrī bandha sarvavighnān hūṃ || Oṃ vajra dṛśya me bhavarakta sarvāvaraṇa svāhā || Oṃ huru 2 hūṃ phaṭ ||
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ.
Oṃ hūṃ bandha vaṃ.
oṃ vajrapāśa hri || oṃ vajrapatāke patani niraṭ || hri vajrakāli raṭ maṭ ||

Oṃ vajraśikhare ruṭ maṭ || Three Conch Shells [image] [page 10] Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ || [image]

Oṃ, the syllable A is the gateway to all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen. Oṃ ā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Bali.
Oṃ vajrānala daha paca matha bhañja raṇa hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrāsane hūṃ || Oṃ sthānaṃ me rakṣa hūṃ, and so forth. Then, with the vajra-cause action-mudrā, one should manifest the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu in front. Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ.
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ || Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ || Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ ||
Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ || Oṃ vajradhātupravarasatkārāya arghaṃ pratīccha svāhā || Argha, pādya.
Rinsing the mouth: *vajrarakṣa hūṃ*. Sprinkling: then the assignment of the flowers:
*oṃ vajradhātu hūṃ*; *oṃ sattvavajrī hūṃ*; *oṃ ratnavajrī trāṃ*; *oṃ dharmavajrī hrīḥ*; *oṃ karmavajrī aḥ*; *oṃ vajrasattva hūṃ*; *oṃ vajraratna trāṃ*; *oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ*.

[Page 15] —

— loke hāṃ || oṃ vajragandhe aḥ || oṃ maitrīspharaṇāya svāhā || amoghadarśine hūṃ || oṃ sarvāpāyaṃ jaha sarvapāpaviśodhanī hūṃ || oṃ sarvasrotasānirghātanamati hūṃ || oṃ gandhahastine hūṃ || oṃ sūraṅgame hūṃ || oṃ gagane gaganalocane hūṃ || oṃ jñānavati jñānaketu hūṃ ||
Oṃ amitaprabhe amṛtavati hūṃ. Oṃ candre candroṣṭhe candrāvalokini svāhā.
Oṃ bhadravati bhadrapāle hūṃ || Oṃ jvālini mahājvālinī hūṃ || Oṃ vajragarbhe hūṃ || Akṣaya akṣayakarmāvaraṇaviśodhani svāhā || Oṃ ||
To Pratibhānakūṭa, svāhā! Oṃ, to Samantabhadra, svāhā!
Oṃ vajrāṅkuśe jaḥ | Oṃ vajrapāśa hūṃ | Oṃ vajrasphoṭa vaṃ | Oṃ vajrāveśa hoḥ.
Indra and the other World-Protectors (Lokapālas)
The fivefold offering of worship.
Oṃ, homage to the offering of the perfection of generosity arising from all Tathāgatas, hūṃ.
[Image] [Page 17] Oṃ, homage to the offering of the perfection of ethical discipline arising from all Tathāgatas, trāṃ hūṃ phaṭ. 2. [Image]
Oṃ, to the offering of the perfection of patience arising from all Tathāgatas, hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
3. Oṃ, to the offering of the perfection of vigor arising from all Tathāgatas, aḥ hūṃ phaṭ! 4.
Oṃ, to the offering of the perfection of wisdom, the Flower-Observer who purifies all miserable realms arising from all Tathāgatas, hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ, arising from all Tathāgatas, purifier of all lower realms, *dhama 2*, *dhumaya 2*, offering of the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*), trā hūṃ phaṭ || 5 || Oṃ, arising from all Tathāgatas, purifier of all lower realms, creator of the light of primordial wisdom (*jñānāloka*), offering of the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhipāramitā*), hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, arising from all Tathāgatas, destroyer of all ill-fortune and odors, offering of the perfection of fragrance, a hūṃ phaṭ.
|| 6 || Oṃ, you who possess conduct beyond compare, whose mind is the essence of equanimity; you whose nature is compassion, the remover of suffering in the world, O All-pervading One...

To the one who bestows the accomplishment of qualities; to the one whose nature is the supreme night of immovable and unchanging equanimity; in the sky-like [expanse] where no protection or knowledge exists; in the subtlest atom of atoms, the stainless; to the one who bestows the supreme accomplishment of the realm of existence and non-existence; in those peerless and all-pervading accomplishments; she is then endowed with the force of stainless compassion; the accomplishment of her vow is unobstructed.
—The nature of reality (*dharmatā*). She who is intent on accomplishing the welfare of the world, whose mind is ever-illuminated by the essence of great compassion;

she who does not waver from the conduct of compassion even toward those who obstruct her, O Vajra, you are the bestower of the supreme accomplishment in the three worlds. Having attained perfect equanimity toward both enemies and friends, oh, how profound is your wisdom regarding the states of the Sugatas! May you grant the boon of the supreme accomplishment of the three samayas.
She who has always attained the state at the forefront of the granting of boons; she who bestows all the supreme accomplishments of the three worlds;
the Protector who traverses the three times and is unobstructed—may the person sounding the bell go forth.
Oṃ, by prostrating with body, speech, and mind to all the Tathāgatas, I perform the vajra-binding.
I offer myself for the worship and service of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, O Vajrasattva of all Tathāgatas, empower me!
Oṃ, I offer myself as a servant for the worship of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, O vajra-jewel of all Tathāgatas, look upon me!
[Image] [Page 21] Oṃ, I offer myself as one who has entered into the worship of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, cause the vajra-dharma of all Tathāgatas to proceed within me!
Oṃ, I offer myself for the ritual activity of worship of all Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, perform for me the vajra-activity of all Tathāgatas!

Oṃ, may all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions attend to me, as well as those abiding in the families of all Tathāgatas, Vajra, Ratna, Padma, and Karma, and all the mudrās, mantras, vidyās, and deities. I, named so-and-so, [in the presence of] all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the ten directions...

In the presence of the Bodhisattvas; in the presence of all the deities of the mudrās, mantras, and vidyās abiding within the Vajra, Ratna, Padma, and Karma families of all the Tathāgatas; and in the presence of all [beings], I confess all my sins in detail throughout the ten directions, for the past and the future.

I rejoice in all the merit of the Buddhas of the past, of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, of the Pratyekabuddhas, of those who have entered the assembly of Śrāvakas, of those who have correctly practiced, and of all classes of sentient beings, throughout the ten pure directions— [including] all the Blessed Buddhas who have not yet set the Wheel of Dharma in motion.
— O Lord, for the turning of the wheel of Dharma in the ten directions, I entreat all the Blessed Buddhas who desire to enter parinirvāṇa: pray, enter parinirvāṇa.
Oṃ, the commitment of the pervasive cloud-mass of flower-offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. || 1 || Oṃ, the commitment of the pervasive cloud-mass of incense-offerings of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. || 2 ||
Oṃ, at the time of the emanation of clouds of light-offering for all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 3.

Oṃ, at the time of the emanation of clouds of fragrance-offering for all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 4. Oṃ, at the time of the emanation of clouds of offering consisting of the jewel-ornaments of the factors of enlightenment for all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 5.

Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive emanation of clouds of supreme offerings consisting of the laughter, joy, and playful sport of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. (6) Oṃ, at the time of the pervasive emanation of clouds of offerings of garments and ornaments for the enlightenment-limbs of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ.
oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇasamaya hūṃ || 8 || oṃ sarvatathāgatodbhavadānapāramitāpūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇe samaya hūṃ || 9 || [page 25]

Oṃ, the samaya of the spreading cloud-mass of offerings of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) that nourishes the unsurpassed awakening of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 10. Oṃ, the samaya of the spreading cloud-mass of offerings of the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) that awakens to the unsurpassed Dharma of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 11. Oṃ, the samaya of the spreading cloud-mass of offerings of the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*) that is unsurpassed within saṃsāra for all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 12.
Oṃ, the samaya of the emanation of clouds of offerings for the meditation on the supreme dwelling known as all the Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 13.
Oṃ, the samaya of the emanation of clouds of offerings for the perfection of wisdom that cuts through the supreme afflictions of all the Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 14.
Oṃ, O all Tathāgatas, destroyers of rebirth in the lower realms, *samaya* of the emanation of clouds of offerings of the perfection of aspiration, hūṃ.
15 Oṃ, O all Tathāgatas, destroyers of the odors of the lower realms, *samaya* of the emanation of clouds of offerings of the Vajra-perfume and the perfection of skillful means, hūṃ.
16 Oṃ, *samaya* of the emanation of clouds of offerings consisting of the presentation of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. 17
Oṃ, the samaya of the emanation of clouds of offerings consisting of the utterance of the speech of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ.
|| 18 || Oṃ, the samaya of the emanation of clouds of offerings consisting of the offering of the mind of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. || 19 ||
Oṃ, O pledge of the spreading cloud of offerings emerging from the secrets of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ!

|| 20 || I offer myself to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; may you accept me at all times and for all eternity. O Compassionate Lords, grant me the accomplishment of the great pledge (*mahāsamayasiddhi*). Furthermore, that root of merit should be made common to all sentient beings. By this root of merit, may all sentient beings—[all worldly... [page 28]

—May they be free from all lower realms and states of suffering. May they be endowed with all mundane and supramundane perfections. Through this very mouth, through this divine joy, may they become Buddhas, the supreme among men. By this wholesome karma of mine, may I soon become a Buddha in the world. May I teach the Dharma for the benefit [of others], and may I liberate beings who are oppressed by manifold sufferings. May one always dedicate [this merit] toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Oṃ.

I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening (bodhicitta), just as the Protectors of the three times have made their resolve for perfect enlightenment. I truly undertake the threefold training in ethical discipline: the morality of restraint, the morality of gathering virtuous qualities, and the morality of acting for the benefit of sentient beings. From this day forward, I shall uphold the vow born of the yoga of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha—the supreme, unsurpassed Three Jewels.
I truly accept the vajra, the bell, and the mudrā; and I shall accept the Ācārya as the Great Vajra.

In the accumulation of the Vajra family, I shall bestow the fourfold gift; and in the Khaṭula family, day by day, in the yoga of the Great Jewel Family and in the delightful commitment (*samaya*), I accept the Dharma—outer, secret, and that of the three vehicles. In the pure Great Lotus Family, which gives rise to great awakening, I truly accept the vow (*saṃvara*) associated with all [families]. In the worship of the Great Action Family, according to my ability, I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*).

Having taken up the vow, O Kṛṣṇa, for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings: those who have not crossed over, I shall cause them to cross; those who are not liberated, I shall liberate them; those who are not at ease, I shall bring to comfort; and I shall establish sentient beings in nirvāṇa.

Immediately thereafter, having performed the consecration of everything preceded by the binding of the mudrās through the application of reflections and so forth, [one performs] the lotus-rotation (*kamalāvarta*) first.
Oṃ, all phenomena are mutually interpenetrating.
Oṃ, all phenomena are established in succession.
Oṃ, all phenomena are seated within the *ate*.
Oṃ, bind the vajra, vaṃ 3.
[page 31]
Oṃ vajrabandha taṭ 3.

[Image] Behold the beginningless vajra by means of the syllable A in the heart. Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra, be firm for me; be eternal for me; grant me your heart; empower me; and accept all my accomplishments, hūṃ ha ha ha ha ho vajrāveśa aḥ.
[Image] Oṃ, all phenomena are mutually interpenetrating; vajramuṣṭi vaṃ 3. [Image]
Oṃ, you who draw out and purify all sins, vajra-samaya hūṃ.
Oṃ, Vajrapāṇi, shatter them! Release all bonds of sin from all states of existence for all sentient beings; O Tathāgata, vajra-samaya taṭ.

Oṃ Vajra Mu || Casting off of Evil. By this rite of offering throughout the incalculable three eons, the yogi becomes visible to the Bodhisattvas. Then, emitting the mantra of Vajrasattva from the center of the vajra located within one’s own heart, one should contemplate the selflessness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmanairātmya*). By means of this [syllable] accompanied by the sixteen vowels, one sees a moon mandala; upon that, with the heart-mantra, one sees the emblem of a white five-pronged vajra with rays of light.
But for others, having placed their respective mudrās, mantras, and signs in the center of the Vajrodbhava, one should cultivate the pride of the mudrā.

—yet || I am Vajra || I am Vajra || I am Ratna || I am Padma || I am Viśva || I am Vajra || I am Aṅkuśa || I am Śava || I am Tuṣṭi || I am Ratna || I am Sūrya || I am Kentu || I am Smirti || I am Padma || I am Khaḍga || I am Cakra || I am Jihvā || I am Karma || I am Dharma || I am Draṣṭṛ || I am Muṣṭi || I am the double Vajra || I am Ratnamālā || I am Vīṇā ||

I am the dancer with sprout-like hands; I am incense; I am flowers; I am light; I am fragrance; I am the hook; I am the noose; I am the chain; I am the bell. Reciting this at one’s own heart, having caused all the Tathāgatas to enter the vajra-realms of body, speech, and mind, one should contemplate their respective mudrās: I am the Vajradhātu; I am Ratnavajra; I am Padmavajra.

I am Viśvavajra. I am Vajrasattva. I am Vajrarāja. I am Vajrarāga. I am Vajrasādhu. I am Vajragarbha. I am Vajraprabha. I am Vajrayaṣṭi. I am Vajraprīti. I am Vajranetra. I am Vajrabuddhi. I am Vajramaṇḍa. I am Vajravāc. I am Vajrakarma. I am Vajradharma. I am Vajracaṇḍa. I am Vajramuṣṭi. I am Vajralāsyā.

"I am Vajramālā. I am Vajragītā. I am Vajranṛtyā. I am Vajradhūpā. I am Vajrapuṣpa. I am Vajradīpa. I am Vajragandhā. I am Vajrāṅkuśa. I am Vajrapāśa. I am Vajrasphoṭa. I am Vajrāveśa. Having spoken thus, one should contemplate one's own heart in the form of one's respective deity. One should visualize the Vajradhātu-maṇḍala complete within one's own heart. Having clearly manifested oneself in the form of Vajrasattva, one should speak as follows:
I am the pledge (*samaya*). I am the pledge; I am like the pledge. Empower me as the pledge-being (*samayasattva*).
Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ. [With a cancellation mark (x) above].

Again, with the vajra-cause action-mudrā, which flashes forth vajra-rays from the moon in one’s own heart, one should emanate the Vajradhātu-maṇḍala in space and behold it. “Thou art the pledge; I am the pledge. Oṃ! Abide, O Vajra! Be firm for me; be eternal for me; empower my heart; grant me all accomplishments! Ha ha ha ha ha ho! Oṃ vajrāveśa aḥ! Behold the two maṇḍalas become one, and behold oneself in space as a formless red [light].

"This beautiful flower garland has been offered by me into the maṇḍala for the sake of the disciple’s entry; may it be so according to the merit of the three families of deities. Whatever [was the nature] of his birth, whatever his lineage, and whatever his place of origin, and whatever the power of the flower—may the maṇḍala be of such a nature! Accept it, O Vajra! Hoḥ! Oṃ, accept this, my child of great strength!"
Oṃ Vajrasattva! You who are intent upon opening my eyes, may you, the Vajra-Eyed One, generate the unsurpassed Vajra-Eye. He Vajra, look! Consecrate me with the vajra! The crown consecration.
Oṃ Vajradhāteśvarī, O Vajrinī, consecrate me; likewise, O Sattvavajriṇī, Dharmavajri, Ratnavajri, Dharmavajrī, Karmavajrī. The crown consecration. [Image] [Page 37]

Oṃ ṭuṃ 2. Oṃ vajra tuṣya ho. Today you have been consecrated as a Buddha by the vajra-name consecration. Receive this state of all-Buddhahood; take it up, O Vajra, for your own benefit. I consecrate you as the Lord of the Vajras; remain firm, O Vajra, for you are the Samaya.

Oṃ, Vajrasattva, I consecrate you with the vajra-name initiation. O Śrī-Śāśvatavajra, Tathāgata named thus, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! This is that state of all Buddhas, which resides in the hand of Vajrasattva. You too must always uphold it, O Vajrapāṇi of firm vow!
Oṃ, abide in the pledge of all Tathāgatas! I hold you, O Vajrasattva! Hī hī hi hūṃ! This is the bell-pledge.

Then, one should contemplate those two as having become one within the four mandalas of one's own heart. Then, while reciting the *samaya* syllable *Aṃ*, [one visualizes] the moon-mandala, and again the moon. With the syllable *Hūṃ*, [one visualizes] a vajra; with *Haṃ*, a vajra. Through the transformation of that, one should cultivate the self as Vajrasattva, white in color, with the pride of "I am he. [With] *Vajrasattva Haṃ*. Having beheld the great body of Vajrasattva, one should explain the Mahāmudrā. Then, one should cultivate the body-mandala: *Oṃ Vajrasattva Hūṃ*.
Visualize the moon mandala in twenty-eight places. This is the seed syllable: Oṃ Vajrasattva Aḥ. Oṃ.
[Page 39]

Vajrarāja aḥ | Oṃ vajrarākṣa aḥ | Oṃ vajrasādhu aḥ | Oṃ vajraratna aḥ | Oṃ vajrateja aḥ | Oṃ vajraketu aḥ | Oṃ vajrahāsa aḥ | Oṃ vajradharma aḥ | Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa aḥ | Oṃ vajrahetu aḥ | Oṃ vajrabhāṣa aḥ | Oṃ vajrakarma aḥ | Oṃ vajrarakṣa aḥ | Oṃ vajrayakṣa aḥ | Oṃ vajrasandhi aḥ | Oṃ vajralāsyā aḥ | Oṃ vajramālyā aḥ |

Oṃ vajragīte aḥ | Oṃ vajranṛtye aḥ | Oṃ vajradhūpe aḥ | Oṃ vajrapuṣpe aḥ | Oṃ vajradīpe aḥ | Oṃ vajragandhe aḥ | Oṃ vajrāṅkuśa aḥ | Oṃ vajrapāśa aḥ | Oṃ vajrasphoṭa aḥ | Oṃ vajrāveśa aḥ. Behold the symbols upon that. Recite "Vajro haṃ" and so forth. Through the transformation of the seed-syllables and symbols, behold the divine pride (*devatāhaṃkāra*). O! In the heart is white Vajrasattva.

To his right is yellow Vajrarāja; to his left is red Vajrarāja; at his back is dark-red Vajrasādhu; on his forehead is yellow Vajraratna; on the back of his head is Vajratejas, with the luster of the sun; and on his shoulders is Vajraketu, [the color of] the sky.

—Bhaṃ. Vajrahāsa, white as a row of teeth, is at the forehead; Vajradharma, white and red, is at the throat; Vajratīkṣṇa, dark blue like the sky, is between the breasts; Vajrahetu, golden yellow, is at the navel; [Vajradharma, white and red, is at the throat]; Vajrabhāskara, resembling a lapis lazuli gem, is on the tongue; Vajrakarma, of variegated colors, is on the head; Vajrarakṣa, golden in luster, is on the shoulders; Vajrayakṣa, black, is on the mouth.

At the hips is yellow Vajrasaṃkṣobhaṇī. To the left of Vajrasattva is white Lāsyā; to the left of Ratna is yellow Mālā; to the left of Dharma is red Gītā; to the left of Viśva is multicolored Nṛtyā. At the abdomen is white Dhūpā; at the head is yellow Puṣpā; at the eyes is red Dīpā; between the breasts is multicolored Gandhā. On the right thigh is white Vajrāṅkuśa; on the left thigh is black Vajrapāśa.

To the right shank, Vajrasphoṭa, white and red; to the left shank, Vajrāveśa, of variegated color. One should thus assign the deities to their respective places. This is the assignment of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). Then, having summoned [the deities] with the Vajra-cause action-seal (*karmamudrā*), [one enters] the great maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

The Uncreated One. Oṃ vajracakre hūṃ. Oṃ vajrasamājaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. [Perform] the vajrāṅkuśa and other mudrās, the water for honor (argha), the water for the feet (pādya), the offering of flowers (puṣpa), the ritual placement (nyāsa), and the praise (stuti). O Pervader of All, who has transcended the Peak of Existence, Lord of the Sugatas, Victor! Great King of the Three Realms, Vairocana, homage be to you! Homage to you, Vajrasattva; homage to you, Vajraratna! Homage to you, Vajradharma; homage to you, Vajrakarma!
Having produced a white five-pronged vajra from the syllable *hūṃ* in one's own heart, one should bind the pledge-mudrā (*samayamudrā*).
